title: The best CloudTalk alternatives in 2026
summary: The best CloudTalk alternatives for outbound sales in 2026, ranked. Artisan runs calling inside one AI-driven system, plus Orum, Salesfinity, Koncert and more.
body_markdown:
The best CloudTalk alternative for outbound sales is Artisan. It runs calling inside one AI-driven outbound system instead of a standalone call-center phone: calls become steps in an AI-run sequence, Ava does the work around them, and pricing is usage-based. For dedicated parallel-dial floors, Orum and Salesfinity go wider.

## Why do teams look for a CloudTalk alternative?


CloudTalk is a capable cloud call-center platform. It gives support and inside teams call routing, interactive voice response (IVR), analytics, and per-seat pricing per its pricing page. Outbound sales teams look elsewhere because of scope. CloudTalk is telephony first, so the outreach around a call, your leads, your email steps, and your reply handling live in other tools. Reps dial in one place and prospect in another. As call volume grows, teams also want faster dialing modes and tighter number-reputation controls than a support-oriented phone system tends to prioritize. When calling is one part of a prospecting motion instead of the whole reason you bought a phone, a sales-native system starts to win.


## How we chose


We ran four tests, weighted for outbound sales instead of support telephony:


-


The tool should cover more than dialing: sourcing, writing, dialing, and reply handling all count.


-


Calls that run as steps inside a sequence beat a separate softphone.


-


Published pricing beats demo-gated quotes.


-


Number pooling, do-not-call (DNC) checks, calling-hours enforcement, and CRM owner mapping matter across a large team.


## What is the best overall CloudTalk alternative?


### 1. Artisan: Calling inside one AI-run outbound system


Artisan is the strongest CloudTalk alternative for outbound because calling is one channel inside a full system. An AI business development representative (BDR) named Ava sources leads from a database of over 250 million B2B professionals across over 200 countries, enriches them with waterfall email and phone data, writes personalized outreach, dials, handles replies from a knowledge base, and books meetings. Calls run as steps in the same multichannel sequence as email and social media, so a dial connects to everything before and after it.


The dialer holds up at enterprise scale. Power and parallel dialing reach up to three lines with AI answer detection, live talking points before the call connects, live transcription, auto-classified outcomes, AI voicemail drop, and automatic area-code matching. Numbers are pooled at the org level with personal callback routing so return calls reach the right rep. Compliance runs per lead, covering calling-hours enforcement, federal DNC checks, consent-aware recording, and carrier spam-reputation monitoring.


Pricing is the sharp edge. Artisan is usage-based, so you pay for the work Ava actually performs: qualifying, enriching, personalizing, and sending messages. Over 90% of customers run Ava autonomously, which is what turns a dialer into an outbound engine.


**Best for:** outbound teams from startup to enterprise that want one AI-run system, with sales ops running Ava centrally for account executives (AEs) who never log in. **Who should pick something else:** teams whose entire day is maximum-volume parallel calling may want a dedicated 5-to-10-line floor. **Pricing:** usage-based, with a free trial and no platform fee. See[Artisan pricing](https://www.artisan.co/pricing) .


### 2. Orum: Enterprise parallel dialing across regions


Orum is the enterprise parallel dialer, running 5 to 10 simultaneous lines with AI answer detection and international dialing on its top tier. It acquired Scout AI in July 2026, extending its conversation-intelligence story. Reported pricing sits around $250/user/month and is gated. For a global, high-volume call floor, it is a capable specialist. For a direct comparison, see[Artisan vs. Orum](https://www.artisan.co/blog/artisan-vs-orum) .


**Best for:** large international teams of sales development representatives (SDRs) that optimize connect rate above all. **Who should pick something else:** teams that want calls as one step in a broader AI-run cadence. **Pricing:** reported ~$250/user/month, gated.


### 3. Salesfinity: Transparent parallel dialing


Salesfinity is the parallel dialer that publishes its price. It runs five lines at $149 or $349/user/month per its pricing page, which is refreshing in a category full of demo gates. For a team that wants a straightforward parallel floor without a sales cycle to learn the cost, it is an easy shortlist entry.


**Best for:** teams that want a parallel dialer with pricing they can see up front. **Who should pick something else:** teams that need the surrounding outbound motion, not just faster dials. **Pricing:** $149 / $349/user/month, five lines, per its pricing page.


### 4. Koncert: Multi-mode dialing


Koncert offers several dialing modes in one platform, parallel, flow, and agent-assisted, so teams can shift between call styles as campaigns change. It leans toward outbound sales instead of support telephony and includes number-reputation features. Pricing is public, a per-seat ladder from Click at $6 to AI Parallel at $99/user/month across five dialing modes.


**Best for:** teams that want to switch between parallel and single-line dialing in one tool. **Who should pick something else:** teams that want an AI to run the cadence around the calls. **Pricing:** $6 to $99/user/month public ladder.


### 5. JustCall: Phone plus SMS for smaller teams


JustCall is a cloud phone and texting platform for small and medium-sized business (SMB) sales and support, with a sales dialer, SMS, and CRM integrations in one app. It is a lighter, more affordable CloudTalk-style option that adds native texting. For a small team that wants voice and SMS without a call-center build, it fits. See also[Kixie vs. JustCall](https://www.artisan.co/blog/kixie-vs-justcall-which-should-you-choose-in-2026) .


**Best for:** small sales and support teams that want voice and SMS together. **Who should pick something else:** teams that need the AI to source and write, not just dial and text. **Pricing:** per-seat tiers, per its pricing page.


### 6. Aircall: Support and inside teams


Aircall is a widely used business phone system with call routing, IVR, a shared number, and a large app marketplace. It overlaps CloudTalk closely on the support and inside-team job. If you are leaving CloudTalk for reasons other than outbound scope, Aircall is the most like-for-like swap. Compare directly in[Artisan vs. Aircall](https://www.artisan.co/blog/artisan-vs-aircall) .


**Best for:** support desks and inside teams that need reliable telephony and integrations. **Who should pick something else:** outbound teams that want a dialer wired into prospecting. **Pricing:** per-seat tiers, per its pricing page.


### 7. Dialpad: AI voice plus meetings


Dialpad is an AI-native business communications platform spanning voice, meetings, and a contact center, with real-time transcription and coaching. Like CloudTalk, it runs a whole company's phones, with more AI baked in. Its sales tier gives reps AI-assisted calling if you want unified communications and a sales dialer under one roof.


**Best for:** teams that want one platform for internal comms and customer calls. **Who should pick something else:** outbound teams that want a dialer inside prospecting, not a unified communications suite. **Pricing:** per-seat tiers, per its pricing page.


## Stay with CloudTalk if...


Keep CloudTalk if the call center is the point. If your team runs support or inside sales that needs IVR, routing, queue analytics, and reliable global telephony, CloudTalk does that job and outbound prospecting is a secondary use. The alternatives above earn their place when calling is one step inside a prospecting motion instead of the reason you bought a phone system.


Chain of Events shows the payoff of consolidation. The team sourced over $700K of annual recurring revenue (ARR) in six months with Ava, a 20x return, running calls as part of the same AI-driven motion instead of bolting a dialer onto a separate stack.

## FAQ


### What is the best alternative to CloudTalk for outbound sales?


Artisan, if you want the dialer inside a system that also sources leads, writes outreach, and handles replies. Calls run as steps in an AI-driven sequence, priced by usage. If your team only needs a high-volume call floor, Orum and Salesfinity are stronger single-purpose picks with 5 to 10 parallel lines.


### Is CloudTalk built for outbound sales?


CloudTalk is built primarily as a cloud call-center phone for support and inside teams. It handles routing, IVR, and analytics well. For outbound prospecting, the dialer sits apart from your leads, email steps, and reply handling, so teams that live in outbound usually prefer a tool where calls are cadence steps instead of a separate phone app.


### What is the best enterprise alternative to CloudTalk?


For enterprise outbound, Artisan pairs a compliant dialer with central-ops deployment: pooled org-level numbers, CRM owner mapping so calls log to the right rep, automatic DNC and calling-hours enforcement, and SOC 2 Type II attestation. Pricing is usage-based, so cost follows the work Ava performs. For a global standalone call floor, Orum's 5-to-10-line dialer with international dialing is the specialist choice.


### How does Artisan's dialer pricing compare to CloudTalk's?


Artisan is usage-based. You pay for the work Ava performs across qualifying, enriching, personalizing, and sending, and the dialer runs inside that same platform. CloudTalk prices per seat by tier per its pricing page. Confirm current tiers directly, since call-center pricing changes often and varies by minute bundles.


### Does Artisan do parallel dialing?


Yes, up to 3 lines with AI answer detection, run as steps inside multichannel campaigns. This covers most outbound teams. Salesfinity runs 5 lines and Orum reaches 5 to 10, so a team whose entire motion is maximum-volume parallel calling may still prefer a dedicated floor.


### Can one tool replace CloudTalk and my sequencer?


For outbound, Artisan can. It runs email, social media outreach, and dialer call steps in one AI-driven sequence, with lead sourcing, enrichment, reply handling, and meeting booking in the same platform. This consolidates the dialer, the sequencer, and the data tools most teams stitch together. It is not a full company-wide call center for support the way CloudTalk is.


## The bottom line


CloudTalk is a call center. If outbound sales is the job, the stronger move is a system that dials as one part of running the whole motion.[Artisan](https://www.artisan.co/) puts calling inside an AI-driven outbound engine, with Ava handling sourcing, writing, and follow-up around every call. For a pure parallel-dial floor, Orum and Salesfinity remain the specialists.
